transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I guess I came in because I can’t stop thinking about my face, mostly the left side. It just looks wrong to me, like my nose and jaw are crooked, especially in ID photos or when I’m on camera for online classes.

And I know people say they don’t notice it, but I don’t really believe that. Like, in the CNC lab, I feel like everyone sees that first before they even notice what I’m doing or the work I’ve done. It’s kind of always in my head.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, taking a lot of photos, or trying to cover up that part of your face?

Yeah… I do. Mostly before I leave for school, I get kind of trapped in the bathroom. I’ll check the mirror, then the front camera on my phone, then the mirror again, because they look different and I can’t tell which one is the “real” one.

I’ll mess with my hair for a long time, or change shirts because some collars make my jaw look worse from the side. And I’ll ask my mom, like, “Does it look weird today?” even though I know she gets tired of me asking.

Sometimes it takes so long that I miss lab, or I get there late and I’m already exhausted, so I can’t really focus on the machines or the programming stuff. Which is frustrating because I actually like that work… but then I’m thinking about how I look instead of what I’m supposed to be doing.
Do these thoughts about your face ever make you feel so anxious or upset that it’s hard to do things you need to do, like going to class or spending time with friends?

Yeah… definitely. I mean, it sounds stupid when I say it out loud, because it’s just my face, but I’ve missed CNC labs and even shop shifts because I’ll be standing there trying to leave and I just… can’t. Like I’ll think, “If I walk in like this, everyone’s going to see it.”

And now my faculty mentor said my work placement could be in trouble, which freaks me out because that’s kind of the whole reason I’m in the program. I used to be pretty good about showing up for stuff, too.

I also stopped playing soccer, which I miss, and I haven’t been volunteering. Not because I don’t want to, exactly… it’s more like I don’t want people looking at me the whole time. Even though they’re probably not, but it feels like they are.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms, including preoccupation with perceived facial defects (left side of face, nose, jaw), repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, photo-taking, reassurance-seeking), and significant impairment in functioning (missing classes, work shifts, social activities) strongly indicate Body Dysmorphic Disorder. Other candidates (F22.8, F40.00, F32.9) are ruled out due to absence of core features like delusional beliefs, primary fear of scrutiny in social situations, or major depressive episode.
